title: Cyclic descent to fixed-ring punctures
statement: Let $R,H$ be commutative rings in one universe and $\iota:R\to H$ a ring map. Assume $H$ is strictly henselian local (henselian with separably closed residue field), $H$ and $H/(\iota(g))$ are regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $\iota(g)$ is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal of $H$, for $g\in R$. Let $n>0$ be invertible in $R$, put $U=D(g)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $j:Y\to U$ be finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $p=j\circ\iota_U$. Put $A=R[T]/(T^n-g)$ and $V=D(g)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$. Suppose there is an isomorphism $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}V\cong\coprod_{\operatorname{Fin}d}V$ [def-pc-fibre-product] commuting with the projections. Then there are $m\in\mathbb N$ and subgroups $K(k)\subseteq\mu_n(H)$ for $k\in\operatorname{Fin}m$, and an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}H$ from $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}H$ to $D(\iota(g))\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_k C^{K(k)})$. Here $C=H[t]/(t^n-\iota(g))$, the rotations and the fixed subalgebras are the actual polynomial-evaluation constructions described in [lem-sbc-strict-local-root-invariants]; no intermediate-root identification is asserted.

proof.text: Put h=iota(g) and C=H[t]/(t^n-h). The monic relation makes C finite free. Its closed fibre has one prime, so C is local and strictly henselian. The root t is regular, C/(t)=H/(h), and the local regularity computation of [lem-sbc-root-algebra-regular-at-root] makes C regular local. It is a normal domain and its puncture is connected.

Hensel lift the residue roots of X^n-1. The n rotations t to zeta*t give a connected cyclic torsor on D(h). Base change the supplied splitting along iota: associativity of pullbacks and the monic-root base-change isomorphism identify the pullback with d copies of this torsor. Its descent datum is a permutation action on Fin d. Partition this finite set into orbits, enumerate them by Fin m, and let K(k) be the stabilizer of a chosen representative.

Torsor descent identifies the component for K(k) with Spec((C[1/h])^K(k)). In a domain with nonzero h, invariance of a fraction forces invariance of its numerator, so this ring is (C^K(k))[1/h]. The finite disjoint union is D(h) in the spectrum of the product of the fixed subalgebras, since finite products commute with localization. All maps are over H, giving theta and its projection equation. For d=0 there are no orbits and the product is the zero ring, with empty spectrum.
